verses.text: Then Pharisees and teachers of the Law rolled in from Jerusalem to talk to Jesus.
They asked, “Why do your disciples ignore the elders’ tradition? They don’t wash their hands before eating bread.”
He answered, “Why do you break God’s command just to protect your tradition?”
“God commanded, ‘Honor your father and mother,’ and, ‘Whoever speaks evil of their father or mother must be put to death.’”
“But you say, ‘If someone tells their father or mother, “The help you could’ve gotten from me is a gift devoted to God,”’”
“then they don’t have to honor their father or mother. You’ve made God’s command empty just to keep your tradition.”
“Hypocrites! Isaiah called it when he prophesied about you:”
“‘These people talk close to me and honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far away.”
“‘Their worship is empty; they teach human rules as if they were my commands.’”
Jesus called the crowd over: “Listen up and understand this.”
“What goes into your mouth doesn’t make you unclean. What comes out of your mouth does.”
Then the disciples came and said, “You know the Pharisees got offended when they heard that, right?”
He answered, “Every plant my Father in heaven didn’t plant will be pulled up.”
“Leave them be. They’re blind guides. If one blind person leads another, both end up in a pit.”
Peter said, “Explain that story to us.”
Jesus said, “You still don’t get it either?”
“Don’t you understand that whatever enters your mouth goes into your stomach and then out of your body?”
“But what comes out of your mouth comes from your heart, and that’s what makes you unclean.”
“Evil thoughts, murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony, and insults against God all come from the heart.”
“That’s what makes a person unclean. Eating with unwashed hands doesn’t.”
Jesus left there and went to the region of Tyre and Sidon.
A Canaanite woman from that region came out, crying, “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! A demon is tormenting my daughter badly!”
Jesus didn’t answer her. His disciples came over and urged him, “Send her away—she keeps calling after us.”
He answered, “I was sent only to the lost sheep of Israel.”
But she came, bowed before him, and said, “Lord, help me.”
He answered, “It isn’t right to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
She said, “Yes, Lord. But even the dogs eat crumbs that fall from their masters’ table.”
Then Jesus answered her, “Woman, your faith is huge! Let it happen just as you want.” Her daughter was healed that very hour.
Jesus left there, went along the Sea of Galilee, climbed a mountain, and sat down.
Huge crowds came to him, bringing people who couldn’t walk, see, or speak, people with injuries, and many others. They laid them at his feet, and he healed them.
The crowd was amazed: people who couldn’t speak were speaking, the injured were healed, people who couldn’t walk were walking, and the blind could see. They praised Israel’s God.
Jesus called his disciples over and said, “I feel for this crowd. They’ve stayed with me three days and have nothing to eat. I don’t want to send them off hungry; they might faint on the way.”
The disciples asked him, “Where are we supposed to get enough bread out here in the wilderness to feed all these people?”
Jesus asked, “How many loaves do you have?” They answered, “Seven, and a few small fish.”
He told the crowd to sit down on the ground.
He took the seven loaves and fish, gave thanks, broke them, and handed them to the disciples. They passed the food out to the crowd.
Everyone ate and had enough. They gathered seven baskets full of the pieces left over.
Four thousand men ate, besides the women and children.
Then Jesus sent the crowd away, got into a boat, and went to the region of Magdala.
